conflicts.description: The advisory table marks five of the eight window endpoints approximate with a tilde and states no error margin, while the conclusion timeline gives nearby exact instants for different events: the release build trigger at 17:47 UTC against the ~17:43 start of the Action windows, and the Docker Hub pushes at 15:43 and 16:34 UTC and the removal at 01:40 UTC against the image window. The exact start of the binary window is an artifact-availability minute, not the first malicious action.
conflicts.rationale: Every endpoint is encoded at the minute the publisher states, with minute precision, the source-rounded approximation label, and the original cells retained, so a reader sees which endpoints are approximate; no reviewer-invented margin is added and the remediation guidance asks for manual review of runs near an endpoint.

conflicts.description: The advisory names safe versions (trivy v0.69.2 and v0.69.3, trivy-action v0.35.0, setup-trivy v0.2.6), the database record names fixed versions 0.35.0 and 0.2.6, and the discussion names two commit objects for the safe Action releases. Version strings are not immutable objects, setup-trivy v0.2.6 carried malicious content inside its window before being re-created, and the named commit objects were retrieved for existence only.
conflicts.rationale: No known-good identity is encoded until reviewers independently verify a specific object; the maintainer safe-version statements are carried in the remediation guidance instead.
